subject: AveryTech QBR prep + renewal risk register — exec attention items
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2028-09-06 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Prep: AveryTech QBR (Sept 12) + renewal risk register

Team —

Quick kickoff for the AveryTech QBR next Tuesday (Sept 12). They`re a mid-market account that expanded in 2027 and are up for renewal in Jan 2029. Leadership wants a tight readout: health, open technical risks, commercial asks, and any exec attention items we should surface.

Primary goals for our internal prep:
- Confirm customer health signals and top 3 risks (ops, performance, contract).
- Review the renewal risk register and score each lane (adoption, cost, reliability, exec alignment).
- Draft 8–10 slide QBR deck and a 1‑page exec summary for our VP.
- Decide on any pre-QBR remediation tasks and owner assignments.

Attachments: initial draft deck and the renewal risk register CSV (see attachments). Please do the following by EOD Thursday (Sept 8):
1) Each of you add 1–2 slides with recommended mitigation(s).
2) Update the risk register scores and add evidence links.
3) Flag any escalation items that should hit exec for sign-off.

Notes: Sara at Avery (cc in later thread) asked for a 30–45 minute joint session; I`d prefer a 45-min joint readout plus a 15-min follow-up with their execs if needed.

Thanks — I`ll consolidate on Friday and loop in Lauren for the VP deck.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: AveryTech_QBR_draft_v1.pptx (pptx, 5MB), renewal-risk-register.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-06 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prep: AveryTech QBR (Sept 12) + renewal risk register

Thanks — quick reads below and I`ll drop slides into the deck by Thursday: 

- Adoption risk (High): usage plateaued on the embeddings pipeline. Marcus, can you add a short remediation plan and owners (eng + CS)?
- Cost sensitivity (Medium): procurement is asking for unit pricing clarity. Neha, want to propose a 6‑month committed cadence and a modeled cost-savings slide.
- Reliability (Low-Med): a couple of latency blips tied to burst traffic; ops fixed but we should include trace examples (timestamp + call id).

Exec asks I think we need: 
1) VP sign-off on a 6-month pricing pilot (if they push).
2) Approval for a targeted SRE intervention (2 weeks of dedicated tickets).
3) Authorization to propose a fallback SLA if they require guaranteed p99 in peak windows.

Also suggesting a one-pager for our CEO-facing exec snapshot — I`ll draft.

—Lauren
VP, Customer Success (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-07 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prep: AveryTech QBR (Sept 12) + renewal risk register

Adding updates on the risk register and a short procurement playbook: see inline.

- Renewal risk register (summary):
  * Adoption: score 7/10 (we`ll detail plateau; usage per seat 9% down q/q). Evidence: internal analytics link and customer-runbook examples.
  * Cost: score 5/10 (procurement is price-sensitive but engaged). Evidence: quote history and marketplace comps.
  * Reliability: score 6/10 (isolated latency incidents, mitigations in place).

Procurement playbook (slide to include):
- Offer: 6‑month committed volume at a 12% discount vs list, with a review clause at 3 months.
- Hook: Provide one-off credits for migration costs (cap $40k).
- Escrow: Standard data handling language; we need legal to confirm retention terms.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.pdf (stub) — I`ll draft MAP and the legal asks and put links in the deck.

Marcus — can you put the ops trace/sample on slide 6? I`ll model the cost sensitivity table on slide 7.

Neha
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: mutual-action-plan.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara.malik@averytech.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@averytech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-09 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AveryTech QBR prep + proposed agenda and asks (Sept 12)

Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for confirming the QBR slot. Attached is a draft of the QBR deck and a short mutual action plan for the renewal conversation. We`ve also included a one-page executive summary for your leadership to review.

Proposed agenda (45 minutes):
1) 5m — Intros / objectives
2) 10m — Health snapshot (usage, stability, support metrics)
3) 10m — Key risks + proposed mitigations (ops, cost, adoption)
4) 10m — Renewal conversation & commercial proposal (6‑month pilot option)
5) 10m — Next steps / owners / dates

Exec asks from our side:
- Approval to pilot the 6‑month committed pricing option (details in slide 7).
- Sign-off on proposed remediation plan for the embeddings adoption work (SRE + CS joint effort).

Can you confirm the attendee list for Sept 12 (we`re targeting 10:00–10:45 PT) and whether you want us to present the exec summary live or send it ahead of time?

Thanks — Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: AveryTech_QBR_draft_v1.pptx (pptx, 6MB), mutual-action-plan.pdf (pdf, 120KB), renewal-risk-register.csv (csv, 15KB)
